transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Nina (GH - Head Data), Tom (GH VP Eng), Aisha (GH Sec Lead), Oliver (GH DevOps)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — retainer uplift, eu vpc status, open security Qs, and action items. is that still good on your side?
[00:12] Nina (GlassHarbor): yeah thanks maya. wanted to make sure we give you the context: traffic spiked 30% q/q and the eu region is a hard requirement for our ad-serving stack due to gdpr flows.
[00:25] Tom (GlassHarbor): hi all, i'm joining from the engineering side — main ask is predictable p99 latency under 120ms for our short prompt renderer. cost also matters — we don't want to double spend.
[00:38] Luis (Redwood SE): got it, p99 120ms target. quick clarifying q: is that cold-start p99 or steady-state with caching?
[00:45] Tom: mostly steady-state, with bursts in the morning. cold start is less frequent but still important for on-call windows.
[00:53] Priya (Redwood CSM): noted — we've seen similar patterns with other media customers, caching + prefix reuse helps a lot.

[01:10] Aisha (GlassHarbor): real quick on security: we'll need kms integration, audit logs at a token-level-ish granularity, and the usual SOC2 artifacts. Also SAML SSO. Can you confirm where logs are stored for private and hosted?
[01:25] Maya: yes — hosted keeps audit logs in our analytics plane with retention options; private / VPC gives you local audit forwarding to your SIEM. we'll send the SOC2 packet after the call.
[01:36] Aisha: okay but need explicit fields: user_id, request_id, model_version, token_count, response_hash. we'll email the canonical list.

[02:05] Luis: on the eu onboarding we spun up a test pool in eu-west-1. initial perf looks good but we need to run it with their exact prompt mix to be conclusive — which is why we requested the sample prompt set last week.
[02:20] Oliver (GlassHarbor): sorry, we dropped that in S3 under gh-prod/prompts/sample-mix.json. i can paste the link in the notes.
[02:30] Maya: perfect. Luis, can you run a 48 hour bench sim with that set and our suggested batching profile and quantization?
[02:38] Luis: yes. i'll run 2 variants: hosted eu pool and dedicated eu-dedicated nodes with nvcalc q8 profile so we can compare cost/latency.

[03:05] Tom: question on contract: we're comfortable increasing retainer but need the ability to burst beyond committed units during campaigns. we'd like a defined burst band and price for it.
[03:17] Maya: we can add a burst clause — typical structure is committed units + 50% on-demand burst at a higher per-token rate, with an upper cap. we can model a-tiered discount if you commit to a longer term.
[03:31] Tom: ok can you put numbers? we need a simple example that shows our current spend -> uplift -> projected savings.
[03:40] Priya: we'll attach a pricing worksheet. maya will draft an amendment with an example 20% uplift and burst band, and we can iterate.

[04:10] Nina: on data residency — some EU customers require data not leave the region. if we use hosted eu nodes, does anything still touch us-east for logs or control plane?
[04:22] Maya: control plane metadata may reside in a global control plane for orchestration, but we do offer an EU-local option for audit logs and payload routing for customers with strict residency. for the private package we can keep everything in your VPC.
[04:38] Aisha: that global control plane is a blocker for a few of our customers — can you produce a diagram and the encryption-at-rest scope?
[04:47] Maya: yes, we'll include diagrams. priya will share the security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/sec/glassharbor-soc2.pdf

[05:20] Luis: technical aside — regarding p99 and batch sizing, there's an observable tradeoff: aggressive batching reduces per-token cost but increases tail latency during low qps. For your morning bursts we can use adaptive batching with a latency ceiling. we'll prototype two profiles in the bench.
[05:40] Tom: sounds good. what about KV cache persistence across sessions? we've seen issues in earlier infra where kv caching wasn't preserved after node rotation.
[05:49] Luis: good point — our runtime keeps KV cache in RAM with optional local checkpointing to NVMe; node rotation can cause cache misses but we have sticky routing and fast rehydrate to mitigate. sometimes it shows up as K-V cash in logs, ha, which confuses devs.

[06:30] Oliver: from ops — peering options: do you prefer transit gateway or VPC peering? we have firewall restrictions on peering.
[06:39] Maya: both are supported; transit gateway simplifies many routes but costs more. for small-scale we often recommend direct VPC peering and IP allowlists. Oliver, can you send your current firewall IP ranges and we can validate?
[06:50] Oliver: will do by EOD.

[10:05] [jumping ahead - mid call detail] Luis: pulled a quick sample bench snapshot: hosted eu pool median token latency ~38ms, p95 ~95ms with default batching; dedicated with q8 quantization median 42ms p95 110ms but cost per token is ~18% lower. that's preliminary.
[10:25] Tom: Interesting — dedicated latency a bit worse at p95, but cost savings are notable. can we shave p95 by tuning kernels or increasing instance type?
[10:35] Luis: yes, kernel selection and larger GPU instances (fewer batch contends) lower tail. we'll add a variant with larger instances in the full run.

[14:00] Aisha: about KMS — we use a managed HSM via our cloud provider and need Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) support. does Redwood support external KMS?
[14:12] Maya: yes, BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted can integrate with your KMS for envelope keys but we'd need an HSM contract review for full key custody.
[14:25] Aisha: okay please send the integration steps and sample encryption flow.

[18:30] Nina: on timing — we'd like the uplift effective for Oct 1st campaign. What milestones do we need to hit to make that happen?
[18:40] Maya: for Oct 1, we need amendment signed by 2027-09-20, bench results by 2027-09-09, security review and KMS answers by 2027-09-12, and if private/VPC is required then provisioning window is 4-6 weeks after sign-off.
[18:55] Tom: tight but feasible. if the 4-6 week provisioning hits, that might push campaign dates. are there fast-path options?
[19:05] Priya: fast-path is staged: start with hosted eu pool (3-5 days activation), then move to private once provisioned. that lets you hit campaign dates while we do the heavy lift.

[22:00] Maya: legal & procurement — any open terms? Tom?
[22:08] Tom: standard SLAs, we need uptime guarantees for dedicated. also request for a lower egress rate for EU-bound data.
[22:20] Maya: dedicated comes with SLA options; we'll provide the SLA matrix in the amendment. egress we can negotiate, we'll put proposed rates in the pricing sheet.

[26:00] [noise / cross-talk] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[26:10] Aisha: one more ask — audit logs retention: some of our partners want 7 years. can you support multi-year retention?
[26:22] Maya: yes — retention tiers available as an add-on. longer retention can be routed to your S3 with lifecycle and encryption.

[30:00] Luis: running through benchmark plan: 48h run, 3 profiles (hosted small, dedicated standard, dedicated large instance). metrics collected: median/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1M tokens, token throughput, KV hit ratio, memory churn. will save raw logs to the bench bucket and summarized csv to the shared sheet.
[30:22] Oliver: sub-question — can bench run with your adaptive batching tuned to 120ms ceiling?
[30:29] Luis: yes that's the second pass. we'll do baseline then latency-capped run.

[34:10] Nina: ok on the commercial ask — we're targeting a 20% retainer uplift with an optional 50% burst band and 12-month term. if you can show net savings vs. current month-to-month, leadership will sign off.
[34:25] Maya: understood. we'll model scenarios and put a simple table in the amendment.

[38:00] Tom: competitor question — Anthropic pitched a server-side solution claiming lower latency in eu. have you benchmarked them?
[38:10] Luis: we've seen mixed results. some models have low medians but higher tail in our tests. we'll include competitor notes but propose focusing on your real prompt mix.

[42:00] Priya: recap — actions: maya to draft amendment and pricing (due 9/6), luis to run bench (due 9/9), priya to send soc2 pack link (done by 9/4), aisha to send audit log spec (due 9/7), oliver to confirm VPC/firewall ranges (due 9/5).
[42:18] Maya: yep and we'll set a follow-up on 2027-09-13 to review bench and amendment.
[42:26] Nina: perfect. thanks everyone.

[47:30] Tom: small note — can you flag any breaking changes during kernel updates? we've had surprises before.
[47:38] Luis: yes we have a rollouts page and automatic fallback. we'll highlight critical compat notes in the bench report.
[47:48] Maya: thanks all. meeting adjourned.
